g-prep-11.reason: 'stay parked ... until the end of next month' = continuing state up to a point. 'by' marks a completion deadline and cannot go with a stative 'stay parked'; 'since' needs a past start; 'from' needs an end point ('from X to Y').
g-prep-11.ldbs: L yes (by passes 'lowered by the end of'); D yes (the deciding word 'stay' is outside the 4-word window); B weak (by/until is a well-known pair, strong students apply it at once); S no.
g-prep-11.why: Medium: L and D pass, B is only partial because by/until is a drilled rule; not hard.

g-prep-12.reason: 'within seven days of receiving it' is the fixed frame. 'in seven days of' and 'after seven days of' are not standard; 'by seven days of' is not English.
g-prep-12.ldbs: L yes (in seven days reads fine locally); D yes (the 'of' that decides it sits after the parenthetical); B yes (in = after seven days is a belief form); S yes (skip 'excluding public holidays' to see 'within ... of').
g-prep-12.why: Hard but only just: the insertion before 'of' supplies the D and S; the within...of frame is well known so a strong student sees it fast.
g-prep-12.editorNote: Borderline hard; if the batch needs a safe hard keep it, but do not call it harder than TOEIC.

g-prep-13.reason: 'at the end of every month' is the fixed phrase; 'never earlier' fits 'at'. 'by the end of every month, never earlier' is odd but not clearly wrong (by = no later than; with 'never earlier' it collapses to 'at'); it is also weakened by 'late transactions are posted until midnight on the last day' (a by-deadline cannot include them). 'on the end' and 'in the end of' are not standard.
g-prep-13.ldbs: L yes (by passes locally); D yes ('never earlier' and the because-clause follow the blank); B weak (at the end of is the reflex choice, so the clue is barely needed); S no.
g-prep-13.why: Medium: the correct answer is the default fixed phrase, so the later clues add little; 'never earlier' reads like a patch added to kill 'by'.
g-prep-13.fix: Replace 'by' with a clearly wrong option such as 'until' or 'before', or drop 'never earlier' and let a different clue (e.g. 'once the last transactions are posted') exclude 'by'.
g-prep-13.editorNote: 'by' is nearly defensible: grammar fine, meaning coherent as 'by the end, never earlier'. Not marked ambiguous because 'never earlier' plus the midnight-posting clause contradict a deadline reading, but an editor could argue it passes. Replace the distractor to be safe.

g-prep-14.reason: 'without a recorded fault for the first six months' (duration). 'by', 'since', 'from' do not fit 'the first six months' here.
g-prep-14.ldbs: L no (no distractor reads right in the window; 'for' is the default); D n/a; B no; S no.
g-prep-14.why: Easy: L fails, nothing locally plausible.
g-prep-14.fix: Rework so two options are locally plausible and the clue is far, e.g. 'has run without a recorded fault ___ the new intake screen was fitted in January' with since / for / from / by, or a since-vs-for-vs-in frame with a later numeric clue. Avoid during/throughout/over as distractors (all acceptable).
g-prep-14.editorNote: Also uses 'by' as a distractor for the fourth time in this batch; 'by' is overworked (items 11, 12, 13, 14, 19).

g-prep-15.reason: Forecast assumed slow sales; 'yet' and a second shift show orders above it, so 'ahead of'. 'in line with' contradicts 'yet' and the second shift; 'in view of' and 'in spite of' do not express a comparison with 'run' (in spite of would need an odd reading, 'run despite the forecast').
g-prep-15.ldbs: L yes (in line with is the classic 'run in line with the forecast' collocation); D partial ('yet' is about six words before the blank, 'second shift' after); B yes (in line with is a believed collocation); S no.
g-prep-15.why: Medium: a classic trap collocation but 'yet' is close to the blank so one clause of reading settles it; closer to a vocabulary set-phrase item than grammar.
g-prep-15.editorNote: Set-phrase/vocabulary flavour rather than pure grammar; fine for the unit.

g-prep-16.reason: 'prior to installing it' fits 'while the part is still in its packaging'. 'subsequent to installing' is grammatical but contradicts the so-that clause (a part in packaging has not been installed): a detail exclusion. 'due to' and 'according to' do not make sense with 'installing it'.
g-prep-16.ldbs: L yes (subsequent to reads fine locally); D yes (the so-that clause is after the comma); B partial (opposite-meaning pair, few believe it after reading the clause); S no.
g-prep-16.why: Medium: L and D pass, B is only partial.
g-prep-16.editorNote: 'subsequent to' is excluded by an in-sentence detail (packaging), so a legitimate trap, not ambiguity.

g-prep-17.reason: 'trimmed its weekly output in response to the outage ... that began last week, rather than waiting for the regulator to order a cut'. 'in anticipation of' is the near second reading: output could have been trimmed before the outage began last week. That requires assuming when the trim happened, which the sentence does not state; 'in contrast to' and 'in return for' do not fit.
g-prep-17.ldbs: L yes (anticipation of passes locally); D yes ('began last week' and 'rather than waiting' follow the blank); B partial (response/anticipation is a meaning pair, not a usage trap); S no.
g-prep-17.why: Medium: L and D pass; B is a pure meaning contrast.
g-prep-17.fix: Remove the timing gap so only 'response' works: e.g. 'the outage at Harbor Point that has now lasted a week' or 'that is entering its second week'.
g-prep-17.editorNote: 'in anticipation of the outage that began last week' is defensible if the trim preceded the outage. Needs an external assumption, so shouldFix, but it is close to ambiguous.

g-prep-18.reason: 'out of stock ... ever since a strike halted production, so the supervisor has asked the Bexley depot' shows no stock. 'in stock' contradicts the later clause; 'off stock' and 'by stock' are not used.
g-prep-18.ldbs: L yes (in stock is the default collocation); D yes (clue is after the comma); B no (nobody holds 'in stock' once the so-clause is read); S no.
g-prep-18.why: Medium at most; the so-clause makes it obvious, so closer to easy in feel.
g-prep-18.editorNote: Feels easier than TOEIC: 'out of stock' is a drilled phrase and the clue is explicit.

g-prep-19.reason: 'as of the first of next month' marks the effective date; claims filed earlier get the old rate. 'by the first' would include earlier claims and contradict 'filed earlier'; 'before' reverses the meaning; 'since' cannot take a future date.
g-prep-19.ldbs: L yes (by and before read fine in the window); D yes ('whereas claims filed earlier' at the end); B yes ('filed by the first' is a believed deadline reading); S yes (work out which side of the date gets the new rate).
g-prep-19.why: Hard: L, D, B all pass, plus a two-step direction check.
g-prep-19.editorNote: 'by' is excluded only by the final clause (legitimate trap). Check that 'by the first' is not read as 'on or after'; it cannot be.

g-prep-20.reason: 'suspended pending the outcome of the safety review' (until it is known). 'following' / 'after the outcome' contradict the relative clause (the review is not finished, so there is no outcome yet); 'regarding' makes no sense with 'suspended'.
g-prep-20.ldbs: L yes (following/after read fine); D yes (the relative clause after 'review' supplies the exclusion); B yes (a suspension following a review outcome is a believed reading); S partial (realise the review is unfinished).
g-prep-20.why: Hard: strong B from following/after plus a distant clue.
g-prep-20.editorNote: Good trap: following/after excluded by 'cannot complete before the end of March', not by assumption.

g-prep-21.reason: 'installed throughout the terminal, from the check-in hall to the farthest boarding gate' = everywhere in. 'through' is not used with 'installed'; 'between' and 'beyond' do not fit.
g-prep-21.ldbs: L yes ('through' passes for some learners in the window); D partial ('from ... to ...' follows the noun); B yes (through for throughout is a real learner confusion); S no.
g-prep-21.why: Medium: L and B pass, D is weak.
g-prep-21.editorNote: 'installed through the terminal' is not standard, so no ambiguity; borderline between easy and medium.

g-prep-22.reason: 'in charge of the pilot scheme once it launches, although he has asked to hand it over' needs responsibility. 'in favor of' is the planted decoy from 'spoken warmly about the plan' but sits oddly with 'once it launches' and 'hand it over'; 'in need of' and 'in case of' do not fit.
g-prep-22.ldbs: L yes (in favor of fits 'spoken warmly'); D yes ('once it launches' and 'hand it over' follow the blank); B yes (the decoy is deliberately planted); S no.
g-prep-22.why: Hard: L, D, B all pass.
g-prep-22.fix: Make the stem less contrived: 'plan'/'scheme' mismatch and the transparent 'spoken warmly' decoy are visible; unify the noun and soften the decoy.
g-prep-22.editorNote: Reads slightly constructed: the decoy clause is too obviously placed to mislead.

overall: No second correct answers found. Bands: 1 easy, 7 medium, 4 hard (hard 33%, within the grammar target; but g-prep-12 is only just hard). Weak spots: g-prep-13 (the 'by' distractor is nearly defensible and 'never earlier' is a patch), g-prep-17 (in anticipation of is possible if the trim preceded the outage), g-prep-14 (easy, nothing locally plausible). vsToeic easier on 14 and 18 (2 of 12, above the one-in-ten ceiling, so replacing 14 and hardening 18 is advised). 'by' is used as a distractor in five of the twelve items and several items (15, 17, 18, 22) are set-phrase vocabulary rather than grammar. Compared with real Part 5 prepositions, these stems are longer and more explicit; real items usually leave less of a clue in the same clause.
